Detail

Educational tool — for information only, not a substitute for proper statistical review.

📖 How to use

  1. Choose a one-sample test (data vs a claimed mean) or a two-sample test (compare two groups).
  2. Type each sample as comma-separated numbers.
  3. Press Calculate to get t, df and the two-tailed p-value.
  4. Read the verdict at α = 0.05 and check the assumption notes.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How is the p-value computed?

From Student's t distribution via the regularized incomplete beta function — the same computation R and SciPy use — evaluated in your browser.

One-sample or two-sample?

One-sample compares your data's mean against a claimed value μ₀. Two-sample compares the means of two independent groups using pooled variance.

What are the assumptions?

Roughly normal data (or n ≥ 30 by the CLT) and, for the two-sample version, equal variances. The tool reports each sample's size, mean and standard deviation so you can judge.
